Messages.Author: Simidh
Messages.Body:
Posted this in the white-wolf forums but figured posting here
might be better as I like that this forum gets archived and so
is a more useful resource in many ways.

If a tapped vampire uses forced awakening to try and block an
action and the block comes via superior version of Kiss of Ra
as opposed to an normal block (ie a card text block versus
a minion block), does the reacting vampire still burn a blood?
Similarly, if I play Kiss of Ra with Toreador using Aching Beauty,
does the attempting blocker still burn a pool? (and yeah not many
Toreadors (if any) have fortitude but is an idea I was thinking
about to get the benefits of both torporing their vampire -and-
make them burn a pool at the same time. ;-)

Simidh, Prince of Adelaide >;->

Messages.Author: LSJ
Messages.Body:
Simidh wrote:
> If a tapped vampire uses forced awakening to try and block an
> action and the block comes via superior version of Kiss of Ra
> as opposed to an normal block (ie a card text block versus
> a minion block), does the reacting vampire still burn a blood?

Yes. He burns a blood if *he* doesn't block (not "if the action
isn't blocked somehow").

> Similarly, if I play Kiss of Ra with Toreador using Aching Beauty,
> does the attempting blocker still burn a pool? (and yeah not many

No. Aching Beauty makes the "blocker" burn a blood (not for the
attempt, for the successful block).
